entity.summary: British Columbia-based centralized crypto trading platform that operated from late 2016 until going permanently offline around September 2019. In 2024 the British Columbia Securities Commission found that ezBtc and its directing mind committed securities fraud by misrepresenting customer-asset custody and diverting customer crypto assets to gambling sites and personal accounts.
entity.notes: BCSC findings state that ezBtc accepted its first customer deposits in December 2016 and went offline permanently in or around September 2019. HEI leaves both launch_date and death_date null because neither statement provides an exact calendar day. The same final findings establish fraud involving false custody representations and diversion of customer crypto assets, supporting scam_rug rather than an unproven allegation-based classification. BCSC identifies 1081627 B.C. Ltd. as incorporated in British Columbia. Regulatory findings and sanctions occurred years after the platform stopped operating and therefore are recorded as post-operation regulatory_action events, not as the exchange death date. Historical sources use both ez-btc.ca and ezbtc.ca forms; HEI preserves both as identity aliases and keeps current URL status unknown rather than inferring DNS continuity.

events.title: BCSC panel found ezBtc and David Smillie committed securities fraud
events.description: The British Columbia Securities Commission panel found that ezBtc and David Smillie perpetrated fraud by lying about custody of customer crypto assets and diverting customer assets for their own purposes, including transfers to gambling sites and personal accounts on other crypto platforms.
events.notes: The findings are dated 2024-08-07 and were published by the BCSC on 2024-08-12. The platform had already gone offline around September 2019, so this event does not set the terminal status date.

events.title: BCSC imposed sanctions following the ezBtc fraud findings
events.description: The British Columbia Securities Commission issued its sanctions decision after the fraud findings, ordering financial sanctions and imposing permanent market restrictions on David Smillie and ezBtc.
events.notes: The BCSC hearing record identifies 2024-11-27 as the decision date; the agency published its sanctions news release on 2024-12-02.

evidence.title: David Smillie and 1081627 B.C. Ltd. operating as ezBtc — Findings
evidence.notes: Official BCSC findings effective 2024-08-07 establish securities fraud. The underlying findings also state that ezBtc accepted first customer deposits in December 2016 and went permanently offline in or around September 2019.

evidence.title: B.C.-based crypto trading platform defrauded customers of $13 million
evidence.notes: BCSC news release summarizes the panel's final fraud findings, including diversion of customer crypto assets and customer losses.

evidence.title: David Smillie; 1081627 B.C. Ltd. operating as ezBtc — hearing details
evidence.notes: Official hearing chronology records findings on 2024-08-07 and the sanctions decision on 2024-11-27, with subsequent appeal applications dismissed in May 2025.

evidence.title: BCSC imposes nearly $20 million in sanctions for crypto trading platform fraud
evidence.notes: Official BCSC release summarizes the sanctions decision, including financial sanctions and permanent market restrictions after the fraud findings.
